Prompt and complete revascularization.recommendation: Prompt and complete revascularization is recommended to treat myocardial ischaemia that may be present in patients with recurrent VT and/or VF.

Bradyarrhythmias.clinical_scenario: Sinus bradycardia with haemodynamic intolerance or high-degree AV block without stable escape rhythm

recommendations.text: Intravenous positive chronotropic medication (adrenaline, vasopressin, and/or atropine) is recommended.
Temporary pacing is recommended in cases of failure to respond to atropine.
Urgent angiography with a view to revascularization is recommended if the patient has not received previous reperfusion therapy.

Bradyarrhythmias.clinical_scenario: High-degree AV block persisting after myocardial infarction
Bradyarrhythmias.recommendation: Implantation of a permanent pacemaker is recommended when high-degree AV block does not resolve within a waiting period of at least 5 days after MI.

Bradyarrhythmias.clinical_scenario: High-degree AV block that resolves after revascularization or spontaneously
Asymptomatic and haemodynamically irrelevant ventricular arrhythmias
Bradyarrhythmias.recommendation: Treatment with anti-arrhythmic drugs is not recommended.

Chronic kidney disease.recommendation: Use low- or iso-osmolar contrast media (at the lowest possible volume) for invasive strategies.
Assess kidney function using eGFR in all patients with ACS.
Apply the same diagnostic and therapeutic strategies in patients with CKD as in patients with normal kidney function (dose adjustment may be necessary).

Diabetes.recommendation: Base the choice of long-term glucose-lowering treatment on the presence of comorbidities, including heart failure, CKD, and obesity.
